findings.summary: closeMenu() never removes the outside-click listener added in openMenu()
findings.mechanism: openMenu() adds document.addEventListener('click', onClickOutside) but closeMenu() only calls document.removeEventListener('keydown', onKeyDown) — the click listener is never removed. Each open/close cycle stacks another 'click' listener on document; onClickOutside keeps firing (harmlessly re-closing) after the menu is dismissed, and listeners accumulate indefinitely across toggles, contrary to the stated requirement to clean up the outside-click listener once the menu is closed.

findings.summary: The click listener that opens onClickOutside is added inside openMenu with no guard against the same click event that triggered the open
findings.mechanism: If the toggle button click event is still bubbling/dispatching when addEventListener('click', onClickOutside) is registered synchronously in the same handler, this particular event won't retrigger it (listeners added during dispatch don't fire for that same event), so this is not an actual bug in modern browsers — included only as a note, not a defect.
